You are a parallel engineering worker on the ESP32-S31 openvela project. Workspace: /home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela. The user explicitly requested parallel agents, prioritizing working hardware/BLE and a coherent final product demo. Read the applicable instructions and evidence. Do not access serial devices, USB/IP, flash either board, reset hardware, start heavy whole-firmware builds, edit maintained source/shared configs, edit the checklist, or modify previous evidence. The root owns board and build sequencing. Rootfs has <350 MiB free; write only to the assigned D-drive task directory. Read existing backups selectively; never recursively search all backups or the entire source tree. Do not expose credentials or dump raw private pairing material. Keep original test failures intact and distinguish separate firmware evidence from same-image integration. No publishing or communication to humans. Produce concrete reviewed files/patches and a concise result, not just an unexecuted plan. The root is building E400 cache-writeback-execution, normal korvo-smp-services with 17 ELFs. E399 started all four AppFS services then CPU0 faulted at Flash-resident esp32s31_writeback_all_locked. E400 moves exactly that helper to IRAM. Do not mutate those inputs. E398 BLE simultaneous advertising/scanning and E393 RPA pairing 20/20 passed, both single-core FLAT. Existing E166 and E159 single-core product demos are archived and verified but do not prove BLE inclusion.

Assigned output directory: /mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/parallel-product-convergence-e401/ble_integration

Investigate the concrete minimal path to integrate already-proven BLE into a coherent product Demo. Read the current product profiles, BLE public APIs and E346/E393/E398 evidence. Determine which BLE capabilities are actually compiled into E166/E159 and the current maintained Demo; do not infer from old tests. Prepare a minimal profile/source patch in your task directory for a usable product BLE path (scan/connect/GATT as applicable to existing UI/service APIs), with host-checkable dependency/resource evidence. Do not add unrequested UI polish or implement fake success. If real memory/configuration constraints prevent direct integration, identify precise blockers and give the smallest implementation that retains the requested real BLE functionality. Deliver a unified diff or candidate files and concise exact build/test sequence for root review. No maintained-tree edits or hardware access.

I’ll trace the maintained profiles, BLE APIs, and E346/E393/E398 evidence, then produce a task-directory-only candidate patch and an exact validation sequence. I’ll avoid hardware, maintained-tree edits, checklist/evidence mutation, and heavy builds.

The product documentation distinguishes the media Demo from the isolated BLE qualification images. I’m checking the actual generated configs and build inputs next, so the proposed integration won’t treat earlier BLE passes as proof that the Demo already contains Bluetooth.

A concrete config constraint is confirmed: the single-core media Demo enables Wi‑Fi, while the S31 BLE controller’s FLAT dependency forbids Wi‑Fi. The current SMP services profile has both radios disabled and can legally add BLE. I’m preparing that additive candidate, with a BLE-only FLAT media variant as the smaller fallback; neither will claim the earlier separate-image BLE tests as integrated Demo validation.

The minimal implementation can reuse `bttool`: it already owns the local Bluetooth service and provides real scan, connect, GATT discovery, read, write, and notification operations. No new UI or daemon is needed. The candidate keeps one BLE owner, bounds GATT resources, and leaves service startup under root’s sequencing. I’m now checking its generated configuration and compile graph without building firmware.

The configuration check caught a real missing dependency: both parent Demo profiles disable RTC, so merely setting BLE would silently omit the controller and `/dev/ttyHCI0`. I’m adding the RTC prerequisites to the candidate and rerunning the check. The first configure attempt also hit the shared ccache path restriction; the rerun will keep cache and temporary files inside the assigned D-drive directory.

The second pass confirmed RTC restores the controller, then exposed one more SMP-only gate: the wireless driver menu also had to be enabled for the Bluetooth driver sources to enter the build. That is now explicit. The final checks cover both symbols and actual planned controller/H4/GATT source files, rather than accepting Bluetooth framework flags alone.

The final generated configs now retain the RTC, controller, wireless driver, H4 device, and GATT path in both candidates, with no unsatisfied dependency warnings. Independent review agrees. SRAM fit remains unproven: the old Demo’s internal-heap headroom was only about 19–36 KiB, and the BLE qualification runs did not measure heap usage. The handoff therefore requires a fresh link and real BLE/MEDIA overlap measurements on the resulting image.

The patch, evidence matrix, resource limits, and exact root build/test commands are written. The remaining host step is CMake’s build-graph generation on D drive. The final configs have already passed independent checks; I’m waiting for the graph checks to finish before closing the handoff.

The proposed SMP path adds one `bttool` application and keeps Wi‑Fi off, matching the current services profile. The FLAT alternative retains HMI, SD, and local MEDIA but explicitly gives up Wi‑Fi. Both use real callbacks and peer payload checks; the handoff also calls out that the tool’s `write_request` is a write without response, so notification and readback must verify it.

The build/test instructions now distinguish startup correctly: SMP starts the four services explicitly, while FLAT uses its existing HMI boot script and must not start them twice. The source and config reviews are complete. I’m finishing the generated application-inventory check and preserving the rejected attempts alongside the final candidate.

The completed intermediate graph confirmed the missing wireless gate really omitted `bt_driver.c`, even though the earlier limited checker reported PASS. I’ve preserved that receipt and explicitly classified it as rejected. The final checker now requires the driver sources and catches nested CMake errors as well as Kconfig dependency failures.

Both final configuration and source-graph checks passed. The SMP graph contains the original 17 applications plus `bttool`, with the real controller, Bluetooth driver, H4, scanner, and GATT sources included. Protected maintained files are unchanged. I’m closing the handoff with the patch, verified host receipts, and the remaining link/SRAM/same-image test gates.

Delivered the reviewed [profile patch](/mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/parallel-product-convergence-e401/ble_integration/ble-product-profiles.patch) and [exact build/test handoff](/mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/parallel-product-convergence-e401/ble_integration/README.md).

- E166/E159 contain **no BLE**.
- Primary candidate adds real `bttool` scan/connect/GATT beside SMP Device/MEDIA: **18 planned ELFs**.
- FLAT fallback retains HMI/SD/MEDIA/BLE but disables Wi‑Fi.
- Both configurations and controller/H4/GATT source graphs passed; private patch replay matched exactly. [Host receipt](/mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/parallel-product-convergence-e401/ble_integration/host-review.json)

Maintained inputs stayed unchanged. No firmware build or hardware access occurred. Link fit, internal SRAM headroom, and same-image BLE/MEDIA validation remain root’s gates after E400.

Root reviewed your config finding. Preserve the full product goal: Wi-Fi plus BLE plus services in one firmware is the integration direction; a BLE-only FLAT variant must not replace that end state. Prefer a coherent SMP additive candidate and inspect existing korvo Wi-Fi/BLE coexistence profile for needed dependencies/resource flags. E400 normal SMP services paired build now passed review (17 ELFs, 7722 inputs, writeback/invalidate helpers and HAL critical section in internal SRAM) and is being flashed; no result yet. Keep patches private and no hardware/build conflicts.
